title: Staged prefetch decider with conservative thresholds and automated rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a conservative, staged 'prefetch decider' that recommends and applies batching/caching profiles with SLO-aware limiters and an automated rollback path. The feature should reduce token cost for steady workloads while never degrading 99th percentile latency beyond configured SLOs. This ticket covers design, implementation, canary rollout, and monitoring/rollback automation for the decider and its circuit-breakers.
acceptance_criteria: Decider computes candidate batching/caching profile per route and outputs a recommended config diff
Staged apply flow can push changes to a 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% traffic ladder with automatic pause/rollback on SLO or error triggers
SLO-aware limiters prevent per-GPU and per-route concurrency from exceeding thresholds derived from historical P99 latency and throughput curves
Anomaly detector flags configuration regressions within 5 minutes of introduction and triggers rollback if configured thresholds breached
Console dashboards show token savings, latency deltas, rollout status, and rollback reasons for each staged cohort
End-to-end tests for canary apply and rollback run in CI and pass on synthetic traffic profiles
tasks: Design config diff format and safe-apply API with immutable apply-id
Implement decider engine: profile ingestion, candidate generation, and scoring heuristic
Add SLO-aware limiter library to runtime agent with token-bucket and percentile projection helpers
Integrate anomaly detector: sliding-window latency/err-rate detector with adaptive thresholds and entropy score
Build canary orchestration: traffic ladder controller, cohort tagging, and gradual route reweighting
Add automatic rollback orchestrator that cancels in-flight changes and restores previous config on trigger
Create console UI view and dashboards for rollout state, metrics, and recommended actions
Write integration tests and run cluster-level load tests (p95/p99 verification) before staging to prod
notes: This approach emphasizes conservative defaults: small initial cohorts, short observation windows, and strict SLO gates. We expect future work to relax thresholds for low-risk routes and introduce ML-based confidence scoring.
acceptance_test_plan: Run synthetic steady, bursty, and cold-start traffic profiles against a staging cluster. Verify p99 latency delta < 5ms for 95% of routes and no increase in error-rate >0.1%. Validate that the rollback path completes within the configured 2-minute window and that token consumption metrics reflect expected savings.
observability_requirements: Per-cohort p50/p95/p99 latency, QPS, GPU concurrency, KV cache hit-rate, token throughput, drop/error counts, and a concise 'rollback_reason' tag emitted when automations trigger. Alerts: cohort_p99_delta > configured_slo_delta for 3 consecutive windows; error_rate_delta > 0.2%
comments: 2025-11-03 Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Drafted design and identified required runtime hooks. High-level tradeoff: prioritize safety over immediate cost savings.

2025-11-05 Marcus Nguyen: Spike finished for limiter primitives. Implemented percentile projection helper and initial unit tests. Observed p99 projection is noisy for low-traffic routes—need min-sample guard.

2025-11-07 Priya Shah (SRE): Ran staging load test with naive decider outputs. Results: token savings ~8% but p99 increased on two high-latency routes. Decider scoring needs route-weighted conservatism and a preflight verification step.

2025-11-09 Marcus Nguyen: Added preflight simulation that replays a minute of traffic against candidate config in a sandbox agent. New metrics show predicted p99 impact. Updated acceptance criteria to require preflight pass for >95% of routes in cohort.

2025-11-12 Marcus Nguyen: Opened PR for canary controller (GH #4821). Requesting design review from Product and SRE. Next: hook anomaly detector and wire up rollback alerts to PagerDuty for high-severity breaches.
